newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Federal Express starts Israel flights.
newsitem.headline: Federal Express starts Israel flights.

text.p: Federal Express Corp on Monday began its first regularly scheduled flights into and out of Israel with a red carpet ceremony at Israel's main international airport.
FedEx will be flying a Boeing 727 with 25-ton lift capacity on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays to connect with the company's European hub at Charles De Gaulle Airport in Paris.

Direct flights will cut delivery time between Israel and major European cities to overnight and shave a day from delivery times between Israel and the United States, said David Bronczek, FedEx's senior vice president for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Bronczek told Reuters that FedEx would be launching a new route in September linking De Gaulle with Dubai, Bombay and Subic Bay, the company's Asian Hub, which would improve delivery times between Israel and Asia.
FedEx has been operating in Israel since 1990 through a local agent but used other airlines, including Israel's state carrier El Al and Air France, to carry packages.

Bronczek said the 30-35 percent compound growth rate of FedEx's Israeli business in recent years "put us over the top to the breakeven point" for operating direct flights. He said FedEx would continue to use other carriers for less urgent deliveries.
He would not estimate the amount of cargo FedEx would be flying through Israel but said he expected the 727 to fly at capacity most of the time.
Direct service will not bring lower tariffs on Israel deliveries, Bronczek said, but the company will now be able to offer a wider range of services than before.
